Several supplied papers address watch-time prediction with distributional or mixture-style modeling. The closest match is a hierarchical exponential-Gaussian mixture model for watch-time distribution prediction, which says watch-time is near-zero-inflated, long-tailed, and multimodal, and proposes HEGM to address variance collapse, component redundancy, and inactive components in a prior mixture network [1]. Another closely related paper proposes a distributional serving interface that learns a joint distribution over four watch states and exposes compact summaries and task-specific readouts rather than only a single watch-time estimate [2].

If you want a more general watch-time regression paper, DADF corrects predictable residual structure in a frozen watch-time predictor rather than replacing it with a mixture model [3], and RQ-Reg predicts continuous values like watch-time using residual quantization instead of a parametric mixture [7].
